title: Analytic: one-sided interface fields at oblique incidence (H_z FDFD, interface sampling)
description:
A plane wave (em_fdfd_hz, H_z polarisation = p) hits a vacuum / glass interface at x = x_int at the angle theta_deg: a y-periodic strip with Bloch ky = k0 sin(theta), CPML along x, a line source in the vacuum, glass of index n_glass from x_int (on a cell edge). Two interface selections of the half space, inside (glass) and outside (vacuum), give one-sided outline samples: least-squares planes through the cells of one side only, extrapolated to the drawn interface, so the jump of E_n is resolved instead of smeared over the interface cells. normal_x / normal_y and tangent_x / tangent_y project the E_x / E_y phasors on the outline. The sweep runs theta_deg over 15-60 deg.
Analytic: D_n and E_t are continuous, so |E_n(vacuum)| / |E_n(glass)| = n^2 and |E_t(vacuum)| / |E_t(glass)| = 1 at every angle; the glass carries the transmitted wave only, so |E_t| / |E_n| there = k_x / k_y = sqrt(n^2 - sin^2(theta)) / sin(theta).
Derived values tab: the one-sided means En2_vacuum, En2_glass, Et2_vacuum, Et2_glass (no reference), then En_jump, Et_ratio, Et_over_En_glass, computed from them (derived values may read the ones listed before them), vs their references; expect ~1 % or better (FDFD dispersion and the face-averaged interface permittivity, first order in k h, plus the one-sided extrapolation, ~0.3 % in the glass). A plain cell mean over the interface cells would miss the n^2 jump by tens of %.
Sweep tab: En_jump, Et_ratio and Et_over_En_glass vs theta_deg with the dashed analytic lines.

parameters.name: ky
parameters.description: Bloch wave number along the interface [rad/m]

parameters.name: L_x
parameters.description: strip length along x (CPML at both ends)

parameters.name: dx_cell
parameters.description: uniform cell size (133 cells per wavelength in the glass)

parameters.name: Et_over_En_ref
parameters.description: |E_t| / |E_n| of the transmitted wave in the glass
